description: AIT* (Adaptively Informed Trees) finds a path and then keeps improving it while it runs (it is *anytime*). Like BIT*, it treats each batch of random samples as an implicit *random geometric graph* (RGG), in which each sample links to its near neighbours. A reverse search from the goal, Lifelong Planning A* without collision checks, computes a cost-to-go estimate `h_con` for every state of this graph. A forward search grows a tree from the start in order of `g + c_hat + h_con` and checks only the edges that come out on top; each edge that fails is removed from the graph, and the reverse search repairs `h_con` incrementally, so the forward search turns away from obstacles. AIT* is almost-surely asymptotically optimal (its cost converges to the optimum) and often finds a first path about as fast as RRT-Connect.

papers.authors: Marlin P. Strub, Jonathan D. Gammell
papers.title: Adaptively Informed Trees (AIT*): Fast Asymptotically Optimal Path Planning through Adaptive Heuristics
papers.venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
